sections.h2: Which Forsyth County offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The Board of Assessors values property and processes exemptions and appeals, and the Tax Commissioner prints the bills and collects the money. The assessors are an independent board, separate from the Board of Commissioners, and the Tax Commissioner does not control either body.

  • Board of Assessors: 426 Canton Hwy, Cumming, GA 30040, phone (770) 781-2106.
  • Tax Commissioner: main office at 1092 Tribble Gap Road in Cumming, with a second office at 1950 Sharon Road, Cumming, GA 30041. Phone (770) 781-2110 or email tax@forsythco.com.

Georgia sets the assessment ratio at 40 percent of fair market value. Millage rates come from the Board of Education and the Board of Commissioners, and the county posts them on the assessors' pages, so ask for the current rates for your tax district.

sections.h2: What does the Forsyth County property tax year look like?
sections.html:
January 1 drives everything: value, owner of record and homestead eligibility are all measured on that date. The calendar below follows the Board of Assessors' own summary.

Forsyth County property tax calendar (Forsyth County Board of Assessors, Key Deadlines)
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value, ownership and use are fixed for the tax year
January 1 to April 1Property returns and exemption filings
Late May to JuneAnnual Notice of Assessment mailed to real property owners
45 days after mailingLast day to appeal or to apply for homestead from the notice
SeptemberTax Commissioner mails and posts bills
November 15Payment due

The assessment notice is informational and is not a tax bill. Legislation in 2025 and 2026 removed the estimated taxes and estimated rollback rates from the notice, which now shows the fair market value and the savings from any exemptions you hold.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Forsyth County tax bill, and what if November 15 is a weekend?
sections.html:
Pay online at forsythcountytax.com by card or e-check, through your bank's bill-pay service, by mail to the Tax Commissioner at 1092 Tribble Gap Rd., Cumming, GA 30040, or in person or by drop box at either office. Checks are made payable to the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner.

In 2026 the due date of November 15 fell on a Sunday, and the Tax Commissioner announced that payments received Monday, November 16 would be accepted without interest. Check the calendar each fall for the same situation.

Only the owner of record on January 1 gets a mailed copy of the bill. If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, it usually pays through a third-party service, but the office says the homeowner is still responsible for confirming that payment arrives by the due date.

sections.h2: What happens if a Forsyth County property tax payment is late?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid after November 15 are delinquent. Interest accrues monthly at the rate set by law, and a penalty of 5 percent of the unpaid balance is added every 120 days until it reaches 20 percent. At 90 days past due the office adds a Fi.Fa. (tax lien) fee of $22.50 on bills under $100 or $32.50 on bills over $100.

  • The Tax Commissioner accepts partial payments, but interest and penalties keep accruing on what remains.
  • A 30-day notice of intent goes out before a Fi.Fa. is issued.
  • The lien is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court and remains in effect for seven years, and it can show on credit reports.
  • A returned check adds $30 or 5 percent of the check, whichever is greater, and later payments must be cash or certified funds.

When taxes stay unpaid the property can be levied and sold. Tax sales, when scheduled, are auctions on the first Tuesday of the month at the courthouse in Cumming, and any money above the taxes owed is held as excess funds for the owners.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Forsyth County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the mailing date of the Annual Notice of Assessment. The 2026 notices went out June 26, 2026, so that year's deadline of August 10, 2026 has passed; the same 45-day rule applies to each future notice, and the exact date is printed on it.

You can file online through the county's property search, by mail to the Board of Assessors, or in person at 426 Canton Hwy. The county says email and fax appeals are no longer accepted, and mailed appeals must be postmarked by the last day shown on the notice. Written appeals should say which process you choose.

  • Board of Equalization, with a later appeal to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, limited to valuation, with an appeal to Superior Court. Fees may apply.
  • Hearing officer, for non-homestead real property and certain high-value personal property, on value and uniformity only.
  • Direct to Superior Court, which needs the Board of Assessors' consent. Fees may apply.

sections.h2: How does the Forsyth County homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
You must own the home, live in it and be a legal resident of the county as of January 1, and you must apply; it is not automatic. Once granted it renews each year until ownership changes or you stop qualifying. Apply by April 1, or during your 45-day appeal window, to receive it for that tax year.

The regular exemption takes $8,000 off the assessed value for county maintenance and operations and fire operations, and $2,000 off the school and state portions. A floating feature freezes your county and fire taxable value at the base year set when you apply, so later increases in value are exempt from those two authorities. School and state taxes still follow current value.

  • Age 65 on or before January 1: full exemption from school general and school bond taxes.
  • Age 62 or older with income under the stated limits: additional school tax relief.
  • Disability and disabled veteran exemptions are listed on the assessors' exemption page.

Applications for regular and 65-plus exemptions can be filed online, by mail or in person. The online portal runs from December through April 1. All applications need a Georgia driver's license or ID matching the property address, and the last four digits of a Social Security number.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Forsyth County house?
sections.html:
Georgia bills the owner of record on January 1, so the seller's name may be on the bill even after closing. The Tax Commissioner asks the seller or the buyer to email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com so the bill can be reissued in the new owner's name. That works for purchases made before November 15 of the tax year.

A new deed also ends the old homestead exemption for the seller's name. The buyer who lives in the house must reapply with the Board of Assessors. After a death or divorce, the new owner must apply in person at 426 Canton Hwy.

If taxes are past due at closing, the payoff includes the penalties and fees above, so ask the Tax Commissioner for a figure good through your closing date rather than relying on the face of the bill.

sections.h2: What are the numbers behind the Forsyth County housing market?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 282,805 people, with 98,879 housing units on 224.62 square miles of land. About 84.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $550,400, and median household income is $143,784.

Median monthly owner costs run $2,525 with a mortgage and $674 without one, and median gross rent is $2,090. About 4.5 percent of residents are in poverty.

faqs.q: When are Forsyth County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 each year. In 2026 the date fell on a Sunday, and the Tax Commissioner accepted payments received on Monday, November 16 without interest.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Forsyth County assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the mailing date printed on the Annual Notice of Assessment. For the 2026 notices, mailed June 26, 2026, that window ended August 10, 2026.

faqs.q: What is the Forsyth County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1, or within the 45-day appeal window after the assessment notice. You must have owned and lived in the home as of January 1 of that tax year.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Forsyth County property tax?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at the legal rate, a 5 percent penalty every 120 days up to 20 percent, and a Fi.Fa. fee of $22.50 or $32.50 at 90 days depending on the size of the bill.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell the county when I sell my house?
faqs.a: Yes, it helps. Email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com so the Tax Commissioner can put the bill in the buyer's name. The buyer should also apply for homestead with the Board of Assessors.
